severity_note: Crash (NULL deref) from any user strategy string with a typo inside a nested parameter; parser_yy.y untouched by 7.0.18.
location_7_0_18: src/libscotch/parser_yy.y:458-464 (mid-rule clears context), :482-488 (error action); file unchanged since 7.0.17
evidence: parser_yy.y:485: 'penvptr->paraptr->nameptr, penvptr->straptr->tablptr->methtab[penvptr->straptr->data.methdat.methnum].nameptr,' reached with penvptr->straptr/paraptr NULL after the mid-rule '($<SAVE>$).strat = penvptr->straptr; ... penvptr->straptr = NULL; penvptr->paraptr = NULL;' was discarded by error recovery. git diff v7.0.17 v7.0.18 -- src/libscotch/parser_yy.y: empty.
review_accuracy: accurate on crash, location and reproducer. Its 'Fix' (guard NULL or restore from saved state) is only half right: a NULL guard loses the parameter name, and the saved state cannot be restored by the final action because bison has already discarded it; the restore must happen when the value is discarded (destructor) or the error rule must move inside the sub-strategy alternative. The context can also be non-NULL but stale (inner method with outer parameter), which a NULL guard does not catch.
first_pass_critique: Status/evidence right. Preferred option A (NULL guard + generic message) is not what the maintainer would want: it prints a different, parameter-less message for the nested case and still lets a stale non-NULL context print a misleading 'parameter X of method Y' (e.g. 'r{sep=(m{asc=b}m{:})}' prints asc of m); it also leaves the leaks of the discarded context untouched. Option B (stack in ParserEnv) is more state than needed. The claim 'd555f2c shows the idiom is a local NULL guard' is a stretch: d555f2c removed a call to a non-existent routine.

fix_options.label: A. Typed <SAVE> mid-rule value with a %destructor that restores the context (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Give the mid-rule value a type (bison >= 3.1 typed mid-rule, CMake already requires 3.8.2) and declare '%destructor { penvptr->straptr = ($$).strat; penvptr->paraptr = ($$).param; } <SAVE>', so that whenever bison discards the sub-strategy context during error recovery or abort, the enclosing method and parameter are restored and the existing error rule prints the right names. Grammar and error rule unchanged, no conflict.
fix_options.tested: Built (0 warnings, 0 conflicts) 32/64-bit; all crash strings above now print the correct parameter/method; Mutation fuzz (repro/common/fuzz.py, 4 default strategies x 600 mutations, seed 1): pristine 2072/2400 sanitizer hits, patched 0/2400 (and 0/2400 with seed 2). check targets pass; test_strat_seq regression case added.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on bison calling destructors for popped symbols (documented since bison 1.875) and on typed mid-rule actions (bison 3.1+; the project's CMake requires 3.8.2 and last_resort files are generated by 3.8.2). Side-effecting destructor must be understood by readers (comment added). No behaviour change on valid input; messages for scalar typos unchanged.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Smallest coherent fix that keeps his single error rule and message; the same %destructor mechanism is what COR-23 needs (commit 3), so the three defects share one design: 'every discarded parser value has a destructor'. Precedent for minimal targeted grammar/lexer fixes: e1700d7 (COR-12), a94688c (COR-25).

fix_options.label: B. New PARAMSTRAT nonterminal with its own error alternative, context restored before YYERROR
fix_options.summary: 'PARAMVAL: $@ PARAMSTRAT {restore; if ($2 == NULL) YYERROR; store}', 'PARAMSTRAT: STRATSELECT | error { $$ = NULL; }'. The error is caught in the state after the mid-rule, where the saved value is still on the stack.
fix_options.tested: Built and run: all crash strings print the right parameter; BUT bison reports 1 shift/reduce conflict on token error in state 78 (PARAMVAL: error vs. reduce of the mid-rule), because both error rules are reachable there. Removing 'PARAMVAL: error' avoids the conflict but makes the scalar-typo message depend on bison default reductions and needs a second errorPrint site.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Plain yacc, no destructor; but either a grammar conflict or a duplicated message and reliance on default reductions.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He does not ship grammars with conflicts; rejected.

fix_options.label: C. NULL-guard the error action and print a generic message (first pass / review)
fix_options.summary: Test penvptr->paraptr/straptr for NULL and print 'invalid value for strategy parameter, line, column' when cleared.
fix_options.tested: Not re-run by me (first pass reports 0/2264 crashes with it); by construction it still prints misleading names when the context is stale but non-NULL ('r{sep=(m{asc=b}m{:})}').
fix_options.tradeoffs: Three lines, but two different messages for the same error class, loses the parameter name exactly when the user needs it (nested strategies), and does not address the discarded context being wrong rather than NULL.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would take a guard for a pure NULL case, but here the root cause is a discarded value; the guard hides it.

our_title: stratTestSave() priorities follow enum order, not grammar; right operands of equal priority unparenthesized
ran: Differential tester repro/COR-13/rt.c built against 7.0.18 internals: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$INFRA/asan/lib ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./rt 2000 7 -> '2000 expressions: 675 round-trip tree mismatches, 97 non-idempotent saves' (was 942/942 on 7.0.17); 3000 42 -> 980/149; 5000 3 -> 1651/262. Example: in '/((24.25)=((edge)%(((levl)*(levl))%(13.75))))?r;' saved as '24.250000=edge%(levl*levl)%13.750000'. Patched: 0/0 for (2000,7), (3000,42), (5000,3). Regression test: test_strat_seq on pristine 7.0.18 lib -> 'saved strategy differs: "(/(vert>(10+2)*3+4-2)?..." vs. "(/(vert>((10+2)*3+4)-2)?..."'; passes on the patched tree.
severity_note: Saved strategies (SCOTCH_stratSave, -vs) change meaning when re-parsed: a-(b-c) -> a-b-c, a%(b%c) -> a%b%c.
evidence: parser.c:564 'static char *               strattestsavepa[2][2] = { { "", "" }, { "(", ")" } };' and :597 'i  = (testptr->data.testtab[0]->testval < testptr->testval) ? 1 : 0;', :601 'i  = (testptr->data.testtab[1]->testval < testptr->testval) ? 1 : 0;' compare StratTestType enum positions (ADD=6 < SUB=7, MUL=8 < MOD=9) while the grammar (parser_yy.y:592-662) gives '+'/'-' one level and '%' a higher level than '*'.
upstream_change: 088a1279 swaps the rows of strattestsavepa; c778efa6 propagates fprintf/stratTestSave errors in the same block

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: swapping the rows fixes the reported example ('(10+2)*3' now kept) and c778efa6 makes stratTestSave return output errors of both operands (parser.c:598-607). Missing: (1) a right operand of the SAME priority needs parentheses since every binary operator is left-associative: a-(b-c) saves as 'a-b-c' (different value), a%(b%c) as 'a%b%c' (different value); (2) the test uses enum order as priority, but '+'/'-' share one grammar level and '%' binds tighter than '*', so a+(b-c) saves as 'a+b-c' and re-parses into another tree, and (a+b)-c saves with useless parentheses (non-idempotent save). 675/2000 random expressions still change tree on round trip. No new bug introduced.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 patch (always parenthesize both operands, drop the table) was correct but discarded his minimal-parentheses display; now that he chose the table, our rebased commit keeps his table and error handling and only adds a grammar priority table (strattestsavepr) and '<=' for the right operand: 3 lines, 0/5000 mismatches. Ours is better on correctness; his intent (minimal parentheses) is preserved. The 'always parenthesize' variant is kept as alt A.

review_accuracy: Diagnosis right. 'Swap the table rows' is insufficient: with left-associative operators a right operand of equal priority needs parentheses ('a-(b-c)', 'a%(b%c)' = different values), and '+'/'-' share a grammar level while the enum orders them (tested variant C: swapping rows alone leaves such cases wrong).
first_pass_critique: Analysis of the associativity/equal-priority problem is right and its rank-based diff works (equivalent to my alternative B). It preferred the minimal-parentheses output although that changes the saved form of every existing conditional ('(vert)>(1)' becomes 'vert>1'), which breaks textual comparisons in users' golden files and PyScotch snapshots for no functional gain; it did not consider the fully-parenthesised form that stratSave() already uses for strategy operators.

location_7_0_18: src/libscotch/parser_yy.y:458-481 (fifth PARAMVAL alternative; store at :478-479); file unchanged since 7.0.17
evidence: parser_yy.y:478-479: '*((Strat **) ((byte *) &penvptr->straptr->data.methdat.datadat + (penvptr->paraptr->doffptr - penvptr->paraptr->dbasptr))) = ($2);' with no test of penvptr->paraptr->typeval.
review_accuracy: Location and impact right; mechanism wrong ('after error recovery'): no error is involved, the grammar simply accepts a strategy (or nothing) as any parameter's value. first_pass_critique: Correct on mechanism and preferred option (check in the mid-rule). Its diff adds a new message 'does not accept a strategy', which is misleading for 'vert=}' (empty value) and duplicates the existing 'invalid value' wording; routing through the existing error rule with YYERROR is simpler. It did not notice that the lookahead set makes the check fire for empty values too.

our_title: No %destructor: strategy and test sub-trees popped on parse error are leaked
ran: repro/run_strings.sh <libdir> runs all reproducer strings through repro/common/st (pristine: $INFRA/asan/lib, patched: $WORK/build/lib). Pristine 7.0.18 (detect_leaks=1): '(m{vert=100}|m{vert=)', '/(vert>1 & ', '/(vert>(1+', 'r{sep=(m{asc=b}m{:})}', and the COR-12 string -> 'LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks'; fuzz: 1913/2400 leaks at parser_yy.y:288. Patched: no leak on any of them; fuzz 0/2400 (two seeds).
severity_note: Leak only on invalid strings; agrees with the review.
location_7_0_18: src/libscotch/parser_yy.y (no %destructor; stratParserParse cleanup :824-828); file unchanged since 7.0.17
evidence: git grep '%destructor' v7.0.18 -- src -> none; parser_yy.y:824-828 'if (o != 0) { if (penvdat.straptr != NULL) stratExit (penvdat.straptr); return (NULL); }' is still the only cleanup.
review_accuracy: accurate; its fix (add %destructor for the strategy and test types) is right but incomplete: it does not cover the method nodes being built (kept in penvptr->straptr / in the saved mid-rule values, not in typed stack values), and 'string value types' need no destructor (fixed-size arrays).
first_pass_critique: Preferred option B (a pending-node list in ParserEnv) is unnecessary bookkeeping; option A's worry about double frees with existing manual frees is unfounded (bison never destructs the RHS of the aborting rule). It did not analyse which nodes are on the stack and which are in penvptr, which is the crux. No option was tested.

fix_options.label: A. %destructor for <STRAT> and <TEST>; <SAVE> destructor frees the discarded in-progress method node (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Ownership invariant: typed stack values own completed sub-trees (destructors stratExit/stratTestExit); penvptr->straptr owns the method node being built; the <SAVE> chain owns enclosing ones; the <SAVE> destructor frees the inner node before restoring the outer; stratParserParse frees whatever is left (in-progress node or completed tree after STRAT reduced). Manual frees before YYABORT stay; the debug internal-error path gets its missing stratExit ($2).
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit, 0 warnings; every leak string above is clean under LeakSanitizer; Mutation fuzz (repro/common/fuzz.py, 4 default strategies x 600 mutations, seed 1): pristine 2072/2400 sanitizer hits, patched 0/2400 (and 0/2400 with seed 2). valid strategies and all check targets unchanged.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Depends on bison destructor semantics for popped symbols and abort cleanup (documented, stable). STRAT (start symbol) stays untyped on purpose: bison destroys the start symbol on accept.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Standard bison practice, few lines, keeps his explicit frees; coherent with commit 2's destructor.

fix_options.label: B. Own the method node on the stack via a typed STRATMETHOD mid-rule value; stratParserParse no longer frees
fix_options.summary: 'STRATMETHOD : METHODNAME <STRAT>{ ... ($$) = straptr; }' so bison frees the in-progress node; remove the free in stratParserParse to avoid a double free.
fix_options.tested: Built and run: fixes the nested leaks but LEAKS the whole tree when the error comes after a complete strategy ('r{...}:' -> 624 bytes) because the STRAT rule has already handed the tree to penvdat.straptr, which is no longer freed; also bison -Wother 'unused value: $2'. Rejected.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cannot distinguish 'in-progress node on the stack' from 'completed tree in penvdat' at stratParserParse time.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: No.

fix_options.label: C. Free only the observed sites (first pass option C)
fix_options.summary: Add explicit frees in the specific YYABORT paths that drop nodes.
fix_options.tested: untested: never complete, the discarded-by-recovery values are not reachable from actions.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cannot fix values popped by bison itself.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: No.

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: zero divisor rejected for both integer (parser.c:433-437) and double (:426-430) modulus, with o=1 propagated to the caller, which reports 'error in mapping strategy'; making the double case an error too (it was NaN, silently false) is a reasonable choice. Missing: INTVALMIN % -1 overflows and traps (SIGFPE) on x86 (ran, 32 and 64 bit); integer literal range (parser_ll.l:137/141/153) untouched.
